publication.subtitle: The global today cards
publication.heroTitle: A clearer world in three cards
publication.heroDescription: Essential science and technology news, simplified.

sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Israeli Settlers Attack Palestinians in West Bank, Injuring 12
cards.content: Dozens of masked Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians and set fire to cars and olive trees in the West Bank, injuring 12 people, including four US citizens. A BBC team witnessed the violence, which is part of a pattern of attacks on the annual olive harvest, with over 120 people injured and one killed this year.

cards.title: Carney Warns of High Stakes in Alberta Independence Vote
cards.content: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney urged Albertans to vote against independence, warning that the stakes are high and turnout will determine the outcome. He also cautioned that separation could be exploited by external forces seeking to break Canada. With early voting already underway, Carney is scheduled to attend pro-unity rallies in Calgary and Edmonton ahead of the October 19 referendum.

cards.title: UK Bans Online Pornography Showing Violence
cards.content: From November 6, it will be illegal in England and Wales to possess or publish online pornography showing strangulation, incestuous relationships, or adults role-playing as children under 16. The new rules aim to curb the normalization of violent and harmful content and help prevent real-life harm.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: New dinosaur species found in Zimbabwe: Musango unveiled
cards.content: Scientists have discovered a new dinosaur species, Musango, in Zimbabwe, which is unlike any found in South Africa. The fossil, a bipedal sauropodomorph, is about 4.5 meters long and weighed 220 kg. It's part of a distinct prehistoric community in Zimbabwe, which has its own unique dinosaur species unlike those found in neighboring countries.

cards.title: US Warns of Growing Foreign Espionage in AI Development
cards.content: US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warns that foreign espionage attempts are a growing concern as the US competes with other countries in the development of artificial intelligence. He says the threat is real and that both US companies and the government need to be cautious, citing a recent case where a Saudi national was accused of installing a recording device at an OpenAI conference room. Clayton leads a White House AI task force that aims to stay ahead of foreign competitors, including China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea.

cards.title: Gemsbok spread in New Mexico since 1960s, climate change may favor them
cards.content: Gemsbok, African antelopes, have spread in New Mexico's dry rangelands since being introduced in the 1960s and 1970s. Climate change could give them an advantage over native wildlife as conditions become more widespread, potentially leading to competition for food and habitat.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Sardinian Village Has High Rate of Centenarian Women
cards.content: A Sardinian village, Bolotana, has an unusually high number of centenarians, with women having an exceptional pattern of survival after age 70. Researchers found that women in Bolotana have a 13.8% chance of living to 100, compared to 3.5% in Italy and 3.6% in the US. The village's historical records, dating back centuries, allowed the researchers to independently verify ages and reconstruct residents' life histories.

cards.title: Medication Reduces Inflammation, Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes Patients
cards.content: Researchers found that a diabetes medication, empagliflozin, changes how certain immune cells behave in the bloodstream, potentially reducing harmful inflammation and cardiovascular risk. In a small human clinical trial, the medication reduced inflammatory cell clusters after just two weeks, with measurable effects. The study, published in the American Heart Association journal Circulation, provides the first direct evidence that this medication can alter specific immune cells in humans.

cards.title: Fat Before Carbs Regulates Blood Sugar in Mice Study
cards.content: In a breakthrough study, researchers found that eating fat before carbohydrates can help regulate blood sugar levels by slowing down stomach emptying and reducing the initial spike. This effect was observed in mice and may be applicable to humans, offering a potential dietary strategy to manage post-meal blood sugar rises, an important treatment target in diabetes.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: Shepherd loses 100 sheep and goats in Indian avalanche
cards.content: In October 2025, a 50-year-old shepherd named Joginder Chand and four others lost over 100 sheep and goats in an unexpected avalanche while migrating through the Jarol Jot pass in Himachal Pradesh, India.

cards.title: India hit by heavy rainfall, orange alerts issued
cards.content: India faces heavy rainfall, with orange alerts issued for Tamil Nadu and South Interior Karnataka. Southern states are likely to experience intense rainfall, flash floods, and waterlogging, while other regions may see thunderstorms and strong winds. Delhi and surrounding areas can expect cloudy skies, light showers, and gusty winds, with temperatures ranging from 18 to 31 degrees Celsius. The weather department has warned of lightning and winds reaching 40-50 kmph, advising residents to be cautious and avoid flooded areas.

cards.title: Floating solar farms expand renewable energy production
cards.content: Floating solar installations are becoming an increasingly attractive option for regions where land is limited. Panels installed on reservoirs and other water bodies can generate electricity while reducing pressure on valuable land resources.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Global film festivals spotlight a new generation of filmmakers
cards.content: Film festivals around the world are giving greater attention to emerging directors and independent productions. Organisers say new filmmakers are experimenting with storytelling techniques and technologies while exploring social and cultural themes.

cards.title: New stadium technology changes how fans experience live sports
cards.content: Sports venues are adopting larger digital displays, real-time statistics and connected services to create more interactive experiences for spectators. The technology is also helping teams analyse matches and improve stadium operations.

cards.title: Music platforms experiment with new ways for artists to reach audiences
cards.content: Music platforms are experimenting with new discovery tools, personalised recommendations and direct connections between artists and listeners. The changes are reshaping how new musicians build audiences and release their work.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Landfill operators ordered to use drones to track odour-causing chemicals
cards.content: Residents in Milpitas, California, have long dealt with strong smells from industrial sites, including a massive landfill. Despite some improvements, the odours still affect many people daily. To tackle the problem, the landfill operators have been ordered to use drones and monitoring systems to track and measure the chemicals causing the smells. This data-driven approach aims to pinpoint and fix issues in real-time, making life more bearable for those affected.

cards.title: UK Chancellor Plans Tax Hike on Banks to Boost Revenue
cards.content: UK Chancellor John Healey is planning to increase taxes on the bank sector, with possible options including reversing a 2023 reduction in the bank surcharge or raising the bank levy. Bank shares fell on expectations of a tax hike, with Lloyds and NatWest dropping over 2%. Some experts argue that banks, which made £15bn in profit in the first half of the year, should contribute more to the government's budget. Healey praised the role banks play in the UK economy, but trade unions and some experts call for a fairer share of taxes from the sector.

cards.title: Small businesses increasingly adopt artificial intelligence tools
cards.content: Small businesses are adopting AI tools for customer support, marketing, document processing and data analysis. Lower-cost AI services are making technologies that were previously available mainly to large companies more accessible to smaller firms.
